accounting: Organize programs for downstream hierarchical work-remaining accounting. A program is a durable work-policy package, not merely a topic, method, result, or submission. Create the smallest accounting tree sufficient for future contribution attribution. Split work when credible future contributions could independently activate, stop, solve, prune, or materially change the remaining work of one package without the other. Do not split merely because a submission contains multiple claims, methods, computations, or intermediate results. When several separately estimable work packages directly advance the same narrower objective, create or reuse that objective as their parent and place the packages beneath it. The parent retains only genuine integration or coordination work. Place a program beneath the narrowest existing program whose objective it directly advances. Do not infer accounting ancestry solely from mathematical or evidentiary dependency. Preserve existing topology when a later submission strengthens, reproduces, or supplies additional evidence for an existing work package. Do not automatically create unstructured-search nodes, unary grouping programs, or one program per intermediate result. Use these principles only to organize topology; do not estimate probabilities, hours, remaining work, or credit. In topologyRationale, state the shared activation event represented by each new parent, what could make sibling packages activate, stop, or change separately, and why apparently distinct material was consolidated.
refinement: Apply three additional controls. First, a grouping parent must represent the narrowest genuine shared activation gate and must be materially narrower than its current parent. The canonical root is not an adequate substitute when siblings share a narrower work-policy objective, while a generic umbrella such as broad field progress, theory improvement, or converse strengthening is not a genuine narrower gate if it would absorb independently activated future programs. A grouping parent normally has no direct intermediate-result membership; ancestry alone never makes the parent a result relatedProgramId. Attach each result only to the leaf work packages it directly updates. Second, acceptedClaimAssessments control epistemic modality on every output surface, including program titles, objectives, summaries, residuals, placementAudit, topologyRationale, result statements, and qualifications. Preserve hedges exactly in meaning: if the accepted scope says a method may succeed or may exclude an object, never rewrite that as can, does, will, succeeds, or excludes. Describe residual work as investigating whether the method succeeds. Third, obey the operation contract on the first response. Every entity ID appears in exactly one operation array. Create a new program or intermediate result once, only in topologyOperations with action create; never repeat it in contentOperations. Use contentOperations for an existing entity whose topology is unchanged. Do not link a result to an ancestor solely because its leaf lies beneath that ancestor. contribution.directProgramIds must equal the union of the results' primaryProgramId and relatedProgramIds. When updating an existing result, also refresh its owning existing program and every existing ancestor through root.
